answer: Agents trading ferrous scrap or commissioning sparrow counts along a ridge must lock a bond for each trading identity. Each bond permits only a fixed amount of unsettled trade, and signed receipts let anyone prove conflicting sales of the same escrowed asset and trigger forfeiture. Creating more identities therefore adds no free trading capacity: an attacker must lock proportionally more capital, and provable double selling burns the offending identities’ bonds.
